h100_real_generation.what: the FAIR apples-to-apples on the same H100: llama-bench tg128 is synthetic and over-states llama vs a real autoregressive single stream. Measured against llama's REAL generation (llama-simple), both producing byte-identical golden tokens.
h100_real_generation.status: at REAL steady state we are 96% of llama (191.4 vs 199.48 — the true gap is ~4%, smaller than the 7% the synthetic bench implies). On the actual task of GENERATING THE GOLDEN SENTENCE (24 tokens) we WIN by +13% (191.6 vs 169.51): llama pays graph-capture overhead on a real short generation, our emitted capture path is leaner. llama's synthetic-bench edge comes from split-K + attention-split numerics that we measured BOTH break our golden token stream — the remaining gap is the price of our correctness guarantee, not missing optimization.

closer_logits.what: correctness differentiator: our two-pass-exact lane holds logits within ~1e-3 of the f64 reference; llama's int8-activation path is looser. We are token-identical to llama AND numerically closer to the true logits — same tokens, better math.

general_fusion_pass.what: a GENERAL register-carried fusion pass in the emitter (fuse_elementwise_chains -> k_fused kernels): F1 fuses arbitrary elementwise chains, F2 absorbs silu in-register — SwiGLU emerges from the general pass, not a template
general_fusion_pass.verified: cuda_elementwise_fusion_lock (9 tests; 4 GPU-numeric =VM on RTX 3060) + H100 runs via examples/emit_fuse_h100.rs: a 5-op int chain byte-exact and the SwiGLU chain silu(A+B)*C f32-exact, emitted as ONE kernel (_fused: 4, _silu: 0, _elem: 0)
general_fusion_pass.bonus: found and sidestepped a latent 1-past-end read in recognize_silu (over-counted loop bound); the fused form loops the chain's true N

levers_tested.what: every real batch-1 speed lever, tested empirically — the hardware wall is measured from four directions, and two committed microbench artifacts guard against re-chasing dead ends

levers.lever: kernel fusion (QKV one launch / RMSNorm+RoPE / combine+qact)

levers.effect: 169.4 vs 169.5 — decode attention is latency-bound, not bandwidth-bound
batch-1 has no reuse to exploit (campaign notes)

levers.lever: megakernel (whole decode step -> ONE cooperative launch, 576 grid.syncs)
levers.effect: 1411.9 -> 1399.9 us/step on the structural probe — noise: CUDA graphs already pre-schedule dispatch, grid.sync costs the same as a kernel boundary, and the 8KB hidden state has no locality to capture against 2.8GB/token of weights

levers_tested.conclusion: the compiler-emitted decode is at the A100 batch-1 hardware wall — the same wall hand-tuned llama.cpp hits. Past it lies a different problem (batched serving, speculative decoding, lower-bit models), not a fair same-model tg128 comparison.

matched_precision_speed.note: apples-to-apples: identical activation precision, identical greedy token (220), faster — the FULL-attention forward (Wq/Wk/Wv/Wo + parallel GQA attention), not a seq-1 V-fold shortcut

correctness_mode.note: the true (f64) token is 2701; llama.cpp's int8-act flips the near-tie to 220. Our two-pass path holds 2701 with logits within 8e-4 of f64 — a correctness mode llama.cpp does not have, at 0.77x of llama's speed.

honest_catch: logit-exact AND fastest cannot both hold: llama.cpp's speed IS its inexactness. Being logit-exact costs ~2x activation __dp4a work across every matmul of the full-attention forward — the 5.36 ms -> 7.55 ms wall-clock gap (186.6 -> 132.5 tok/s). We win each axis, not both in one config.
